reviews.title: An Ad for Every Bite!
reviews.text:
I really like this app! It works great with Apple Activity, which is exactly what I want. Unfortunately, the pop-up ads are out of control. 
I open the app to enter my food, and BAM! An ad. I start entering my dinner, and BAM! Another ad right in the middle of it. Some ads don’t even have a close button, so I have to close the entire app, reopen it, and start the whole circus over again.
It literally took me five minutes to enter my dinner. At this rate, I’ll need to log my breakfast before I eat it, just to make sure I finish entering dinner before bedtime! 
I understand the need for ads, but when it takes longer to fight the ads than to log my food, something has gone terribly wrong. I’m tracking calories, not training for an Olympic event in closing pop-up ads!

I started using this one after looking up which is the best for free, and this definitely is. Timestamps are locked but that’s fine, you can still track your weight and what you ate and at what time of day. I’d say the layout is really simple to use, I got used to it really quick. You can even track things down to vitamins or even just moving around the house rather than full workouts, which I think is a lot more inclusive than only counting a gym trip or something as exercise. Personally, I don’t use it, but I think that along with the vitamin levels or even ‘labs’ and ‘mental’ tracking could greatly help someone disabled and trying to keep things in order or get more fit. I’m definitely gonna keep using it seeing as it doesn’t charge anything for its basic use.

reviews.title: Best food/nutrition tracker EVER!! 🙌

And the drag and drop functionality is amazing. I also love that I can get a pretty in-depth analysis of my average nutrient intake, excluding incomplete or empty days where I don’t track. It’s really helpful in determining what supplements I actually need, instead of wasting a bunch of money on stuff my body is already getting from my diet. If you can figure things out on your own, it’s totally worth the money. If you ever need help, good luck.

reviews.title: Way better than MyFitnessPal
reviews.text:
I used MyFitnessPal for over a decade, but I recently discovered Cronometer, and I’m honestly impressed by how much more value it provides for free.

Features like barcode scanning, which MyFitnessPal used to offer for free but now puts behind a paywall, are still included. Cronometer also gives you much more insight into your nutrition without immediately pushing you to upgrade.

I liked the app so much that I chose to upgrade to the Pro version. That’s how an app should work: provide so much value that people want to pay for the premium version, rather than making them feel forced to upgrade just to keep using basic features.

Two great things I don’t see mentioned as often: 

1. Their website is a perfect companion to the app. Of all of the main trackers I have tried, Cronometer’s website looks and works the best. I use it almost as often to log food, especially at work. 

2. Being able to import recipes from URL and automatically sync them with friends has been a game changer. My wife and I take turns cooking and almost always follow a recipe online and it has allowed us to both track calories and lose weight together without much friction. 

Only cons: I don’t think the background app refresh works or it is very infrequent. So if I workout with my watch and it syncs to Health, I don’t think the app’s widgets are updating until the next time I open the Cronometer app.

reviews.title: I like this app - it’s been helpful for my health goals.
reviews.text:
Real person review here.
I’ve been using this app on and off for the past couple years, and it’s been my favorite nutrition/calorie counter so far.
I like the different options of logging in food, especially the barcode scanner. I don’t use the premium version, so I can’t comment on the features it provides. However, using the free version I’ve been more than satisfied. I don’t mind the occasional ads, because they’re super quick and they keep things like that barcode scanner free. (Which I’ve seen other apps put behind their paid version, and why I don’t use them.) 
In addition, this app has a huge database of food for information (uses multiple sources, which you can toggle if needed), so it’s a rare event when I have to personally login a new food. 
And a different feature I like is that I can set my goal weight, and see and choose from options that tell me how long until I can meet that goal. 
It also shows me daily macronutrient goals (protein, net carbs, fat) for target weight as well as balance options. I can also see a further breakdown of my nutrient summary whenever I want to check in the daily report section, which is interesting. 
The UI is pretty easy to navigate, though you need to take a little time to learn where you have to tap/swipe to find the more detailed info. But after using it for while, I can comfortably see/find the info and option these days with no issue. 
Speaking of issues, I did have one earlier today where I was not being shown search results for manually looking up food to add (barcode option was working fine), but after a message to tech-support through their “contact us” in the app, I got a reply very quickly and the problem was resolved within a couple hours. And now everything is working again. The fast response and turn around is what’s prompted me to make this review after all this time. 
All in all, I’ve been very satisfied with the app and how it’s been working so far, and I would recommend it to anybody who needs to keep track of their macros/nutrient intake.

reviews.title: Siri Doesn’t work & Customer Service is nonexistent.
reviews.text:
I purchased the Gold tier subscription as a way to track my raccoon’s caloric intake.  I am visually impaired, so being able to tell Siri what to log would have been very beneficial. The problem is, the app was just creating foods on its on and not using the foods I have listed and created in the Custom foods folder Example: I asked Siri to “log 15 Temptations” ( cat treats) The app logged 1 Met-Rx Big 100 Bar, Super Cookie Crunch. That is not even close to what I said. It was doing the exact same thing with his almonds. I’d say “log 3 almonds”. It would automatically log roasted and salted almonds even though the almonds I have in his foods list are unsalted. 

 I contacted customer support less than 2 hours after I purchased this app to ask for assistance. Then a second time after that. The third time I requested my money be refunded. It’s been over 3 days and I haven’t received a response from anyone. Just 2 emails that say, “Your support request has been updated”. I never received an email in response to my request for a refund. 

So, if you’re wanting this app, so you can use Siri, you’re wasting your money. I paid to use that feature and that feature alone, but I am still just using the free version.

reviews.title: I don’t usually write reviews, but…

The image search feature has been shockingly accurate and has made it so much easier to track what I eat. And the barcode feature has not missed once for me. Plus, it’s all gamified in just the right way to motivate me to work towards my goals. So far, I’ve gained over three pounds and it’s only been a week and a half. Which doesn’t seem like much to some, but considering I’ve put in months of work with no distinguishable change, I’d say that’s pretty huge for me. 10/10, would recommend.
